title: Teaching himself guitar from the tuning fork and book
summary: After two years in Chicago he finds the diagram book and tuning fork in the guitar box and tunes it himself; a friend wants to buy it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: So, I kind of give up on that guitar. I'll just let it stay there. I got it in a big box. You see? And just the way that box come, I set that guitar around in there. I didn't see that guitar in the morning for about two years. I went away. I went to Chicago and I stayed in Chicago about two years. I come back from Chicago and I was working out at a lumberyard called Otis Lumberyard. And it rained one day out there and the weather was cold. And they knocked us off from work, you see? And I come on home. And I got home. There was nobody living in the house between me and my mother. When my mother was working, well, that left me being in the house by myself. So, I made me a big fire. This stone, in the old time greats they call it. Oh, yeah. Made me a big fire and I just sit down there like that. And the only light in the room was the light from the fire. So, I had been sitting down there reading a magazine and I'd been read it so many times. I almost knew it by heart. I thought it in the corner. And I happened to look over and I saw the guitar. I hadn't put my hand on that guitar in about two years, like I told you. I went and I got the guitar and I pulled it out of the box. And when I pulled it out of the box, I kind of tilted the box. When I tilted the box, a little book fell out of there. And inside of there they had something else in there. I didn't know it was in there. You've never seen that. They had a little tuning. They had what you call a tuning fork. Yeah. They had that in there. So, I looked at it and I saw letters on there, you see. So, I thought, I said, well, what is this for? So, then I began to read the book. Well, the book tells me what it's for. That's the sound of each string. So, I took the guitar out and I blowed that and I tuned up the string. And this little book was a diagram book. It shows you where to put your fingers out, you see. So, I sit down there and I figured out how that should be done. But, you know, just doing it by myself, I didn't know if it was right or not. Well, I got the guitar in tune, but I didn't know it was in tune. So, there was a friend of mine, about two days after that, he asked me about the guitar. He said, don't you have a guitar? I said, yeah. He said, well, what, are you learning how to play it? I said, well, no, I don't. He said, well, if you don't learn how to play, why don't you sell it to me? He said, I need a guitar. I told him, I said, well, all right, come take a look at it. So, he picked up the guitar and he strummed it, you know. He said, well, who tuned it up? He said, well, I was a bit surprised, you know. I said, it's in tune? He said, yes. I said, well, I tuned it up. He said, well, I thought you said you couldn't play. He said, well, I can't play. So, he wanted to buy the guitar for me. He said, how much you want from me? I said, well, I didn't say I wanted to sell it. I said, but if you want to buy it, I'll sell it to you for six dollars. He said, well, okay. He said, I'll give you a dollar and a half now and I'll give you a dollar and a half Saturday. I said, well, I don't want to sell it like that. Okay. Well, he said to me, he said, well, you want to learn how to play? He said, I'll help you out with it. All right. Well, by not selling that guitar to him, if he had maybe had six dollars to give me, I probably wouldn't have been playing music today. You see? But he gave me a few ideas on to get drunk and I just began to build them up. Build them up. And I'd get around some places where these friends of mine played piano and I'd strum behind them until I began to get an ear for changing chords. And I just kept on going like that.
